gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its 'Best value' pick, the Sun Gold Power 4000W 12V split-phase LF inverter (LFP4K12V240VSP), needs 240 VAC input to charge or pass power through. Its stated AC input range is 140–270 VAC or 184–253 VAC, so a 120 V-only source such as a 30 A RV pedestal or a 120 V generator falls below it. AIMS sells the same 4000 W, 12 V, 120/240 V split-phase class in two input versions, one for 240 VAC (PICOGLF40W12V240VS) and one for 120 VAC (PICOGLF40W12120240VS).
standout_why: I compared against the two cited Victron pages (help-me-choose and MultiPlus-II 2x120V) and also read the uncited MultiPlus-II 2x120V description page (rank 2). They cover only Victron. They say the 2x120V inverts 120 V only and passes 240 V through only from a split-phase source, and ChatGPT's answer already repeats that, so the Victron limit is not new. None of the 18 results is a Sun Gold Power or AIMS page. ChatGPT's answer never mentions what AC input voltage either low-frequency unit needs, even though its closing question ('both sides of an RV's 120V panel') points at exactly the 120 V-shore setup where the Sun Gold unit cannot charge.
decides: For a 12 V shopper whose only AC sources are 120 V (RV shore power, a 120 V generator or a van), ChatGPT's 'Best value' Sun Gold LFP4K12V240VSP cannot charge or pass power through, because 120 V is below its stated 140 VAC input minimum. The pick then becomes the AIMS 120 VAC-input version (PICOGLF40W12120240VS / PICOGLF4012120240VS). The Sun Gold unit or the AIMS PICOGLF40W12V240VS fits only when 240 V grid or generator power is available. Victron MultiPlus-II 2x120V 12 V models do not produce 240 V from the battery at all.

findings.value: Two 120 V units in a split-phase configuration over VE.Bus, or an autotransformer making 120/240 VAC from a 120 V or 240 V input
